1.2: 1.2 RABANUS. And Ahaziah fell. The house of Ahaziah is the Synagogue, which was surrounded on all sides by the precepts of the law as by the lattices of an upper chamber. But as Ahaziah, falling through the lattices by which he ought to have been guarded, incurred a grievous sickness, so also the Jew, going beyond the guard of the law, fell into the hopeless languor of sins. There, because he abandoned the defence of God, he found no remedy of salvation. For like an impious king he fled to false gods, and therefore is rebuked by the prophetic mouth, and his approaching death is foretold. Ahaziah signifies especially the princes of the Jews, who, given to vices, persecute the truth; whence: The rulers and the Pharisees sent ministers to apprehend Jesus, etc. (John 7).
1.9: 1.9 And he sent to him a captain of fifty, and the fifty that were with him. RABANUS. The captain of fifty is the confession of penance, by which the remission of sins is declared. The Jews therefore, unwilling that Christ be God, or the prince of penance, say to him: Thou hast not yet fifty years, and hast thou seen Abraham? and in the future they are burned with fire. The third captain of fifty, because converted to the faith of the Trinity, knew the sacrament of penance and deserved indulgence.
2.2: 2.2 It came to pass. RABANUS, on the book of Kings, vol. 3. The whirlwind, that is, a very strong wind, etc., until The Lord was taken up, neither begetting nor begotten, by coming together.
2.9: 2.9 Let there be. Elijah excelled greatly in prophetic spirit and in the working of miracles; Elisha therefore asked that the twofold grace which he knew to be strong in his master be granted to himself. Whence it is clear that he did not ask to be a disciple above his master. RABANUS. The Church, having received confidence of asking from the Lord, asks the spirit of Christ, and because she needs the remission of sins, which Christ did not need, and the gift of virtues, which Christ bestows from his fullness through the Holy Spirit, who ascending on high led captivity captive, and gave gifts to men (Ephesians 4), to those, namely, who place their hope in him. Hence it is that he says:
2.10: 2.10 If thou see. That is, if you open the eyes of faith, and with the passion and resurrection faithfully believe also my ascension, you will obtain the effect of your petition.
2.13: 2.13 The mantle. RABANUS. It is the incarnation by which he broke the river of Lethe and prepared for us a passage to life; this Elisha kept after the passing of Elijah, because the Church after the ascension of Christ has kept the faith of the incarnation, through which she strives to cross the waves of the present life; but as Elisha divided the waters only by invoking the name of Elijah, so the Church can do no miracles unless by invoking the name of Christ. For it is God who worketh in us both to will and to accomplish.
2.17: 2.17 Bring. ISIDORE. Salt, that is, wisdom placed in an earthen vessel, that is, the human body, heals the waters, that is, makes the peoples fruitful through the sweetness of love and good works by the incarnation of Christ.
2.23: 2.23 And he went up. ISIDORE. Elisha, salvation of God. He is the one who is called Saviour, whom the Jews mock, because at the place of Calvary he was to ascend the cross; but Christ, after he ascended into the heavens, as Elisha went up to Bethel, that is, to the house of God, in the forty-second year sent two bears from the forests of the Gentiles, namely Vespasian and Titus, who cast them down with cruel slaughter, and there their blood was shed where they hung the Lord.
3.1: 3.1 RABANUS. The three kings warring against Moab are the rulers of the faithful, who through faith in the Trinity fight with spiritual arms against the prince of the world and his people, that is, philosophers, heretics, schismatics and all the wicked. Moab is interpreted from the father; it fits those to whom the Lord said: You are of your father the devil (John 8). These oppose the Church with threats, persecutions and deceit: but through Christ, who is the head of Christians, they are put to flight.
3.16: 3.16 Make. RABANUS. The prophet by a miracle took counsel for the people wearied with thirst, and the words of prophecy give counsel to the faithful how to refresh the mind with spiritual teaching. The same. He makes a ditch in the bed of the torrent who seeks deep mysteries in the Scriptures. These are filled with water without rain and wind; because often without human consolation divine power confers wisdom on those who search. Whence John says: You have no need that any man teach you, but as his unction teacheth you of all things, etc. (1 John 2). Whence: Men and beasts shall drink, that is, they shall receive the teaching, the clever and the simple.
3.18: 3.18 And a small thing. The same. For it does not suffice for the servants of God to know hidden mysteries: they ought also to preach them to others and to refute those who contradict, to whom is promised certain victory over the enemy, that they may strike every city.
3.19: 3.19 City. RABANUS. The city is worldly prudence, in which philosophers and heretics trust; this is overthrown by preachers. Wood. The same. Not that which bears fruit, but the deadly kind, which, cut down at the coming judgment, will become fodder of eternal fire. The springs of waters are stopped, when the heresiarchs with their followers are condemned by Catholics. The choice fields are covered with stones, when the charm of heretical and philosophical speech is overwhelmed by the weight of anathema. Only the earthen walls remain, that is, false reasonings, which are reduced to nothing by the slingers, that is, the holy preachers. RABANUS. So philosophers, thinking the word folly, deride the passion of Christ, and consider the martyrdom of the Church madness.
4.1: 4.1 A woman, etc. RABANUS. Holy Church is the mother of two peoples, that is, Jewish and Gentile, etc., until For Abraham and Sarah received and fed three men.
4.18: 4.18 And the child grew. RABANUS. So the Israelite people, after it had grown in Egypt, and led out through Moses into the desert had heard the voice of the Lord, when it should have been illumined by the light of the sentence, soon, its mind running back to idolatry, died.
4.29: 4.29 And he. The same. While the Lord, etc., until by the spirit of love the boy returned to life.
4.38: 4.38 The sons of the prophets. That is, of preachers, who walk in the law of the Lord and search his testimonies; they live always in the presence of the Saviour.
4.39: 4.39 He cut. RABANUS. He who, intent on the letter of the law or zealous for philosophy, taking bitterness from the law or the deadly from the philosophers, mixes it with the evangelical truth, and in the pot of the heart cooking such a stew, prepares such a teaching for his hearers. For the Apostle says: The letter killeth, but the spirit quickeneth (2 Corinthians 3). And: The wisdom of the flesh is death; but the wisdom of the spirit is life and peace (Romans 8). The faithful, sensing this, cry out, Death in the pot; but meal is put into the pot, when spiritual knowledge is put into such a seasoning, so that, the bitterness being excluded, the food becomes wholesome.
4.42: 4.42 And a man. RABANUS. The man is the company of the fathers: who is from Baal-shalisha, because he keeps the three in the confession of the Trinity. For Baal-shalisha is interpreted having a third. This man offers to the man of God loaves of firstfruits; when, inspired by the grace of the Redeemer, he offers books composed on the origin of creatures. He offers new grain in his bag; when he brings forth the new testament in the writings of the Gospel and the apostles. Our Elisha commands the ministers, that is, the preachers, to distribute these to the faithful, and to bring forth from their treasure new things and old, which mystery we read in the Gospel in the breaking of the five and the seven loaves, where, the crowds being satisfied, they gathered twelve baskets, or seven baskets, of fragments, because no one grasps the sacraments of Scripture in every respect, when something will remain over for him who is satisfied, according to the word of the Lord.
5.1: 5.1 Naaman, etc. RABANUS. He signifies the Gentiles, holding the principate by the strength of wars and enjoying the splendour of possessions. Hence Naaman is interpreted their comeliness or their commotion: a strong and rich man, but a leper; because although he seemed to rule by power of kingdom and abundance of possessions, yet through the error of idolatry he appeared foul with leprosy.
5.2: 5.2 Now out of Syria. The same. Robbers from Syria, etc., until as the chief priest did in the Gospel. The same. And whom the Lord foreknew, them he also called, etc. The Gentile people coming to the house of Elisha, etc., until because the baptized must be confirmed by participation in the Lord's body.
5.17: 5.17 I will take a burden. The same. Naaman took a part of the holy land with him to put in the temple of the idols, and standing on it to adore the Lord whose land it was, lest he offend his Lord if he did not adore equally.
5.20: 5.20 Gehazi. The same. Precipice, etc., until this is the dog returned to his vomit.
6.5: 6.5 But it happened. RABANUS. When the presence of Christ, working through the body, cut down the impious Jews like unfruitful trees; whence: Behold the axe is laid to the root of the trees. By them, with the passion intervening, the body itself was abandoned: it descended into the depths, being laid in the sepulchre as the iron to the handle, and when the spirit returned it rose. The same. Great care must be taken lest the understanding grow numb in idleness, or fade away in the exercise of work through the vice of elation. GREGORY. The iron on the handle is the understanding in the heart: with this the wood is cut, when those who act wickedly are rebuked. But when this is done carelessly, when the lapse of vainglory is not avoided, the iron is lost in the water, because from dissolute work the intelligence is made foolish, which is given for this, that by good action it may be restored before the eyes of the giver, whence follows: This very thing. The elect, however, if ever they offend, return quickly to the heart and pursue their fault with tears, whence: Alas, alas, etc. Weeping, they carefully consider not only what evils they have committed but also what good they ought to have rendered from the gift received, and this is: Alas, alas, alas, and this was borrowed; as if he says: That I lost through the dissolution of negligence which I received by the grace of the Redeemer in order to repay it by good works: but God never abandons the mind which truly acknowledges itself in sins. Hence Elisha cast the wood downward and brought the iron to the surface, because the Redeemer humbles the heart of the sinner and restores the understanding he had lost. Whence in another translation it is said: He broke the wood and cast it in, and so lifted the iron. To break the wood is to crush the heart from elation, to cast it to the depths, to humble it by thought of one's own weakness. Immediately the iron came back, because the understanding runs back to the use of its former exercise.
6.14: 6.14 And when they were come. The same. Whoever, trusting in the arms of wickedness, prepares ambushes for the servants of Christ, blinded by the night of perfidy, wages war against the Church.
6.15: 6.15 Alas, alas, etc. GREGORY. Here he notes those who from faint-heartedness fear bodily punishments.
6.16: 6.16 Fear not. Fear not them that kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do. More. The same. I can ask my Father, and he will give me presently more than twelve legions of angels. Lord, open. The same. It is very necessary that our Elisha open the eyes of the heart to consider that all who trust in him will not be confounded.
6.18: 6.18 Strike. The same. It is good that the scandalizing eye be plucked out, so that the gaze of pride and malice may be stopped, and the eye of sound faith and simplicity opened. RABANUS. After Elisha led the enemies into Samaria, he did not allow them to be killed, but, preparing a meal for them, sent them away in peace. And Saul, long kicking against the goad, the Lord first blinded, then enriched with spiritual knowledge. And he commanded us thus: Love your enemies, do good to them that hate you (Luke 6).
6.24: 6.24 He gathered. RABANUS. Ben-hadad and his army are the devil and the wicked, namely pagans, Jews and heretics, whom he stirs up to wage war against the Church. By such the people of God, placed in Samaria, that is, in the guarding of the law, is afflicted: and famine comes when teachers are not permitted to preach the word of God. But Elisha revealing, that is, the Redeemer showing through the Gospel, the salvation which is far from sinners is known to be near to those who fear God. For the Lord says: Tomorrow a measure, etc. A measure of fine flour is the perfect measure of divine wisdom which is in the New Testament. Two measures of barley are the knowledge of the law and the prophets, which are compared to one stater, that is, the Catholic faith, in the gate of Samaria, that is, in the apostolic preaching, through which one enters the Church. For when the whirlwind of persecution which now occurs ceases, the Lord will give tomorrow, that is, in the future time, tranquillity, so that preaching may be perfectly fulfilled.
6.25: 6.25 And there was a famine, etc. AUGUSTINE, sermon 211, on the seasons. While a wicked nation departs from the worship of God, it is oppressed by dreadful famine and troubled by just necessity. Why, most wretched one, do you suffer famine? Why are you torn by so great a want? The punishment of famine grows daily, because guilt grows daily. The scourges persevere, because in the people sins persevere. Henceforth avoid sins, restrain offences, turn to God, leave the idol: then you will be able to conquer enemies with divine help. And no one will be able to harm you further, if, crime being condemned, divine worship has sprouted in you. Shame! The sinful people feeds on dreadful carcasses and dove's dung, and does not seek the worship of God. Famine and necessity demand polluted flesh and horrid foods; and still hardness worships its fabrication. Piety is turned into food, offspring received is changed into fodder. Parricide is committed before one comes to the deadly feasts. Innocent blood is shed so that the raging hunger of parents may be fattened.
7.3: 7.3 Four, etc. RABANUS, on the book of Kings, vol. 3. They are lepers, etc., until let them preach the truth of the faith in the four parts of the world.
7.17: 7.17 But. The captain holds the type of the Scribes and Pharisees, to whom the Truth says: Woe to you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites; because you shut the kingdom of heaven against men; for you yourselves do not enter in, and those that are going in you suffer not to enter (Matthew 23). Whom the people trod upon in the gate, because he hindered the step to the faith of those entering: whence rightly trodden down, that is, condemned by the judgment of the just judge, he will be sent into everlasting darkness.
8.7: 8.7 Ben-hadad, king of Syria, etc. The king of the Syrians, when he had come to Damascus, and recognized that the Divinity had sent fear and flight upon him and his army, and that it was not done by an attack of enemies, was greatly afflicted, because he had God so angry, and fell into sickness.
9.1: 9.1 Go. RABANUS, on the book of Kings, vol. 3. It designates the principate of the Gentiles, which the Lord appointed to destroy by vengeance the sacrilegious city that killed the prophets and the Lord of the prophets and persecuted his apostles, and to destroy the priesthood which after Christ it had held in vain, and overthrow the temple, and also cast down from the summit of the kingdom the impious Synagogue, which always thirsted for the blood of the saints, and kill its rulers.
9.29: 9.29 And he reigned. RABANUS. It is said of Ahaziah, etc., until and he reigned one year.
10.15: 10.15 Is thy heart right, etc. From this it is clear that even among the tribes there were some men endowed with piety, for whose sake the Lord took care also of the others.
11.1: 11.1 And Athaliah. RABANUS. Athaliah, who sought to destroy the seed of David, expresses the impiety of the Synagogue, which lay in wait for the seed of David, that is, of Christ. She at one time seemed to reign, when she observed the ceremonies of the law temporally. For Athaliah is interpreted temporal of the Lord. But by the vigour of Jehosheba, which is interpreted fullness of the Lord, that is, of the Church, in which are true delights, Joash is preserved, that is, the memory of the Lord. Christ, namely, in whom is the memory of the name of the Lord, lest he be destroyed in the hearts of the elect by the cruelty of the raging enemy. He is further nourished in the house of Jehoiada, which sounds beloved of the Lord, of whom the Father says: This is my beloved Son (Matthew 3), whose house is holy Church, where, abiding in the holy faith of the elect, he daily makes increase of his body, until at the time of judgment he will lift up the sceptre of the kingdom and his power against those who thought to depress him, and will assign the slayer of the saints to eternal punishments.
11.4: 11.4 And the seventh year Jehoiada the high priest sent, etc. The courses of priests, Levites and doorkeepers were twenty-four, and they had as many high priests, who in turn succeeded one another, each for one week, each having under him twenty-four priests and as many Levites, and doorkeepers of the same number. When the new high priest entered upon his office on the sabbath with a new company of priests, Levites and doorkeepers, the high priest with his company who had served during the past week returned home after the sabbath to his wife; for as long as they ministered they abstained from conjugal acts, remaining in the porches around the house of the Lord until the sabbath. But then the high priest, because of the need of increasing the force, retained also those who had completed the week, and took in those who were about to complete it. He also gathered other Levites from the cities and the heads of families, whom, about to bring out the king's son, he arranged in such a way that those who had completed the sabbath should stand around the king armed in the inner places of the court. Those who had come for the sabbath should guard the house of the king, that is, the palace, and the gate of the shield-bearers by which one went down from the temple to the palace. The rest of the multitude should guard the outer gates of the courts against the fury of the queen, if she attempted anything: afterwards he brought out the king from the house of the Lord where he had been hidden, and they came by the way of the gate of the shield-bearers into the palace, and he sat upon the throne of the kings.
11.6: 11.6 At the gate. RABANUS. In the palace the gate of Sur and the house of Messa seem to be the ones named together with the gate of the shield-bearers. Of the shield-bearers, and you shall keep the watch of the house. The same. The shield-bearers were the king's protectors guarding the vestibule of the palace.
11.12: 11.12 And he put upon him the diadem and the testimony. The same. In the book of Chronicles more openly: And they put upon him the diadem, and gave into his hand the law to hold. And it was certainly of saving prudence that, after the killing of the tyrant queen, to the king's son succeeding to the kingdom, together with the very attire of the kingdom, the discipline of the law of God should be committed to be kept: and he who saw himself set over the people to rule should remember that he himself ought to be subject to be ruled by the divine laws.
11.17: 11.17 Jehoiada therefore made a covenant between the Lord, etc. In Chronicles, between himself: because he put himself in the place of the king and of God, whose minister he was; whence Jehoiada is interpreted recognizing the Lord or loving: because he taught to know and love the Lord. He made a covenant between the Lord and the king and the people, that the king and the people should serve the Lord: he made it between the king and the people, that the people should act faithfully toward the king, and the king rule the people with justice.
12.1: 12.1 RABANUS. Our king commands that the teachers receive all the money which is brought into the treasury of the Lord by the passing just of spiritual knowledge or good examples, or that the offices of the preachers be brought to the restoration of the spiritual temple, so that whatever they find there torn through error or vices they may restore, lest perhaps through the negligence of the masters the multitude of hearers perish.
12.5: 12.5 The repairs. The same. He speaks of the ruins of the house of the Lord, that what had begun to fall might be propped up. For it is read in Chronicles that Athaliah and her sons, that is, the priests of the idols (for it is read that she had no son), destroyed the house of the Lord, and of the sanctified things made Baal.
12.6: 12.6 Until. The same. Before the coming of Christ, although the teaching of the law was in the Jewish nation, yet through the negligence of the teachers it was corrupted in many things, until he himself came who gave the law, and taught that through faith in the holy Trinity the decalogue in the writings of Moses and the prophets must be observed spiritually.
12.7: 12.7 Give it for the repair of the temple, etc. The same. The Lord says to the evangelical teachers: Preach the Gospel to every creature, heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers; freely have you received, freely give (Mark 16).
12.9: 12.9 And he took. The same. Our high priest, who offered himself as a victim to God, set up one chest, that is, he made one Catholic Church, in which he opened a hole in the top, because he prepared from there a passage to the heavens. And he set. The same. The altar is the body of the Lord, beside which is the chest, since the Church is joined to Christ at the right hand of those entering the house. Because those who enter the Church by faith intend to reach eternal blessedness, which the right hand signifies. The priests, therefore, who keep the doors of the temple, put in there all the money which is brought to the temple, when the preachers, who guard the entrance of faith, offer the vows of the faithful in words and works: and in the Church duly commend them to God by prayers.
12.10: 12.10 The king's scribe, etc. The same. The highest are the teachers, who gave the money collected according to number and measure to those who were in charge of the carpenters and masons, that is, to the dispensers of the word of God, who gave the measure of evangelical wheat to their fellow servants, those who work in the house of the Lord and put together the works of virtues in the divine building. The same. The apostles, whom divine election appointed princes in the Church, through the disciples scattered the seeds of the word throughout the whole world, so that they might set over their hearers suitable workmen of the will of God, of whom some made wood, when they strove to prepare themselves and those obeying them as fruitful trees in the house of the Lord. Others made the repairs of the temple, when they rebuilt what had been broken by heresy and schisms; others cut stones, when they strongly rebuked the hard of heart and unbelieving, so that the restoration might be fulfilled in all things that needed expense to fortify the house of the Lord, according to that: But to every one of us is given grace according to the measure of the giving of Christ (Ephesians 4).
12.13: 12.13 But there were not made. The same. The method of forming the vessels for the service of the Lord must be one thing, that of preparing wood and stones for the building of the house another, because the teaching by which the unlearned are imbued for the faith must be one, and another that by which the already perfect are instructed to the fullness of knowledge. The vessels of the Lord are those who are already fit to receive divine gifts and are suited for the ministry of God. There were not made. In Chronicles: When they had finished all the works, they brought before the king and Jehoiada the rest of the money, of which were made the vessels of the temple. There is no contradiction, because the vessels for the ministry of the temple were not made from the same money which was offered by the people for the restoration of the house of the Lord, but from the remaining part of the money, which had been collected in other donations too. And the flesh-hooks, etc. RABANUS. The teachers, whose office is to distribute the body and blood of the Lord to believers, to refuse it to unbelievers, and also to apportion spiritual nourishment of the word to each as is fitting: because among the words of God which he has deigned to reveal to our lowliness, there are others which surpass the measure of our capacity. Censers. The same. There are those who offer to God clean prayer from a pure conscience and unfeigned faith and say: Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight (Psalm 140). Every vessel of trumpets, etc. The same. The teachers, who send out through the whole world the voice of the evangelical preaching, whence: Lift up thy voice like a trumpet (Isaiah 58).
12.15: 12.15 And no account was asked of those, etc. The same. They were so religious that no one doubted that they handled the money of God without fraud. Hence it is clear how much discretion is needed by those who dispense the money of the word of God to their fellow servants, for which an account must be rendered, that these may be found no less faithful in spiritual things than those in bodily.
12.16: 12.16 But the money for sin, etc. The same. Here it is shown that the confession of sins and penance is to be carried out not by the judgment of each one but of the priests, whose task it is to discern between clean and unclean and to judge the stain of leprosy.
13.14: 13.14 Now Elisha. RABANUS. Our Redeemer commands the rulers of the Church to clothe themselves with spiritual arms and to fight against the ancient enemy. The bow is the sacred utterance, which consists of both Testaments as of horn and string. By the Old Testament the horn is figured, on account of its hardness; by the New, which was made when the Lord was incarnate, the string is figured: and while the string is drawn the horn is bent, because when the New Testament is examined the Old is bent from its rigidity to spiritual understanding. The arrows are the words which teachers bring forth. We, therefore, when we weigh the sayings of sacred Scripture, bend the bow; when we give words of doctrine, we shoot arrows.
13.16: 13.16 He put. The same. By his own examples the Lord directs and strengthens the actions of teachers.
13.17: 13.17 Open the window. The same. He exhorts his own first to be illumined by the light of knowledge, and so to shoot the darts of words. The arrow. The same. Holy preaching is a most certain slaying of spiritual enemies if it is carried on perseveringly, whence a teacher ought not through avarice to neglect the care of souls, but rather through piety to stretch forward to eternal rest, which Aphek signifies: for it is interpreted he will contain or he will seize, whence the Apostle, having listed vices, added: But thou, O man of God, flee these things, and pursue justice, godliness, and lay hold on eternal life (1 Timothy 6).
13.18: 13.18 Take. Who when. The same. Teachers are commanded to strike the earth with the dart of preaching, etc., until Faith without works is dead. RABANUS. The resurrection of the corpse, etc., until and rather to have a place there than here.
14.1: 14.1 In the second year. And he did. RABANUS, on the book of Kings, vol. 3. Amaziah did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, but not with a perfect heart: for he did good works that please God, but not with a perfect heart, because he showed them before men under a feigned appearance, and so before God they were not acceptable.
14.7: 14.7 In the valley. The same. It was the Valley of Salt, where they made salt. Either by cutting, drying and burning the briny mud; or by boiling the salt waters of wells and cooking them down to the hardness of salt; or by any other method by which salt is customarily made. The rock. The same. Petra is a famous city of Arabia in the land of Edom, which in the book of Numbers is called Rekem, and so called by the Syrians. But Josephus does not say a city but a great rock set in Arabia. Joktheel. RABANUS. The name which Amaziah the conqueror imposed is interpreted assembly of God or help of God, as he faithfully acted so that it might seem to be of present memory that he took it either with the assembly of the people of God or with God's help.
14.25: 14.25 He restored the borders of Israel, etc. Of Jeroboam he says: He restored the borders of Israel from the entrance of Hamath unto the sea of the wilderness. Hamath, which is now called Epiphania, was the northern boundary of Israel. The sea of the wilderness is the Dead Sea, which extends in breadth five hundred and eighty stadia to Zoar of Arabia, in length a hundred and fifty, as far as the neighbourhood of Sodom. Jeroboam therefore encamped against the Syrians and devastated their whole province as Jonah had prophesied. Which is in, etc. Hepher was a tower not far from the temple, of enormous size and height: hence it is called Hepher, that is, of darkness, or of cloud: because it raises its head to the clouds, and is called in Zechariah the cloudy tower.
15.1: 15.1 In the twentieth year Azariah. RABANUS, on the book of Kings, vol. 3. He is Uzziah, etc., until above it is called the gate of Ephraim.
15.35: 15.35 He built. RABANUS. Jotham built the high gate of the house of the Lord, which in the Acts of the Apostles is called Beautiful, and by the Hebrews is called the Gate of Jotham.
16.3: 16.3 He consecrated. RABANUS. Ben-hinnom, son of Hinnom. Topheth or Tophet is in the valley of Ben-hinnom near Aceldama, a place formerly most pleasant, where they used to sacrifice to demons. In Hebrew Gehennon, that is, the valley of Hinnom; whence in the Gospel it is called Gehenna, because as those who worshipped idols perished there in body and soul, so sinners who pass to hell will be punished with eternal damnation.
16.18: 16.18 And the Musach. RABANUS. It is a building placed in the vestibule of the temple, where the kings, when they went to the temple on the sabbath, put in alms; and so the Musach of the sabbath is the treasury of the kings, as the corban is of the priests. The Musach also, etc. RABANUS. He did not turn it to the temple of the Lord because it served the worship of God there, but that it might be profaned with the temple, seeking to please the king of the Assyrians rather than God, so that when he came there, seeing it, he might covet it and take it away, as with many other things Ahaz gave him, that he might find favour with him.
17.27: 17.27 You have brought. RABANUS. The king of Assyria, that is, the devil with his army, afflicts the ecclesiastical people daily, besieging and devastating, when on account of sins committed he tears them from their own seats and carries them into a foreign land. Whence: By the rivers of Babylon there we sat and wept, when we remembered Sion.
17.29: 17.29 And every nation. The same. In the Book of Places it is read that Benoth and Nergal were cities which those who had crossed from Babylonia built in Judea. Ashima also was a town built by those who had come to it from Hamath. Nibhaz and Tartak are cities which the Hivites founded in Judea. The same. It seems, according to the sequence of the discourse and the idols which these nations had served before, that the names can be understood here, because when it had been said: And every nation made its own god, as if to complete the sentence it is added: For the men of Babylon made Succoth-benoth; that is, tents: Benoth, which is the name of an idol. In what follows Adrammelech and Anammelech are shown to have been the idols of the city of Sepharvaim; so it seems consequent that Nergal of the Cuthites, Ashima of the Hamathites, Nibhaz and Tartak were the idols of the Hivites.
17.33: 17.33 And when. RABANUS, from the Euch. Heretics have certain sacraments in common with the holy Church, until and we understand grandchildren.
18.1: 18.1 In the third year. Hezekiah. RABANUS. Seizing the Lord, or the strength of the Lord. For our Redeemer, the Lord strong, the Lord mighty in battle, not only crushed the idols of the Gentiles and scattered the worship of idolatry so that they might have knowledge of the one God and be worthily devoted to his worship: but even crushed the very letter of the Mosaic law, which that legal people echoed with assiduous reading and held in great esteem, and taught them to understand the spiritual sense in it.
18.4: 18.4 And he broke. Hezekiah broke the serpent, because he hoped in the Lord God, not in the brazen serpent. He called it Nehushtan, etc. Which is interpreted their brass, so that they might recognize that what they worshipped as a deity was, in the words of Scripture, metal, not God.
18.17: 18.17 Rabshakeh. RABANUS. Because he speaks Hebrew: they think he was the son of Isaiah who was a traitor with Shebna; or a Samaritan, and therefore knew the Hebrew language. He, like a contrary strength, imitated the prophets with his arrogance. The prophets say: Thus saith the Lord. He said: Thus saith the great king, the king of the Assyrians.
18.18: 18.18 Eliakim. RABANUS. Of this Eliakim Isaiah said: I will call my servant Eliakim (Isaiah 22), who was high priest after Shebna: whom the Hebrews relate, terrified by the threats of Rabshakeh, betrayed Jerusalem, and the Assyrians took the whole city except the citadel as well as the temple; some also assert that Shebna went out to Rabshakeh with Eliakim.
18.21: 18.21 Dost thou trust. No history relates that Hezekiah asked help from Pharaoh.
18.22: 18.22 In the Lord. RABANUS. It is true that they had trust in God, but it is false that Hezekiah took away the high places and altars of God: for he did this not against God but for God, that, the old error destroyed, he might command God to be adored in the temple of Jerusalem.
18.23: 18.23 I will give you. The same. Rabshakeh, to show the fewness of the besieged, promises two thousand horses, for which Hezekiah would not have riders: this comes not from the weakness of the people as though ignorant of riding, but because God commanded that the king of Israel should not multiply horses and wives for himself.
18.25: 18.25 The Lord said. The same. To what he said, If you shall say, We trust in God, he craftily answers that he came not by his own will but by God's, who said: Go up. And the argument is: since I have taken many cities, and part of Jerusalem remains untouched, it is clear that I have come by the will of God.
18.26: 18.26 We beseech thee. The same. The sense is, etc., until which had a likeness to the land of Judea, both in situation and in fruits.
18.29: 18.29 Let not you, etc. The accusation of Rabshakeh is a testimony to Hezekiah, that, evidently when cities were taken, he trusted in the Lord: and he strengthened the people to hope in the Lord. Hence Rabshakeh wishes to destroy what he built, and says to the people: Let not Hezekiah deceive you, and let him not make you trust in the Lord your God. RABANUS. He shows that the Samaritans served the gods of these cities or nations, etc., until as our interpreter has rendered it.
19.1: 19.1 RABANUS, on the book of Kings, vol. 3. Wonderful is the humility and prudence of the king, etc., until and that the enemy would die in his own land.
19.9: 19.9 And when he had heard. The same. By God's will Rabshakeh abandoned the siege of Jerusalem, and found his lord either having taken or abandoned Lachish, attacking Libnah. Sennacherib, meeting the king of Ethiopia, sent letters to Hezekiah that he might terrify by speech those whom he had not taken by force. Herodotus relates that Sennacherib fought against the Egyptians and besieged Pelusium, and, the mounds already built for taking the city, Tirhakah king of Ethiopia came to help. RABANUS. Before, Hezekiah, terrified by fear of the Lord, did not dare adore in the temple or pour out prayers freely there; now, Isaiah saying: Fear not for the words which thou hast heard (Isaiah 41), he boldly beseeches the Lord.
19.21: 19.21 The virgin daughter. RABANUS. Because, all the nations adoring idols, she alone preserves the chastity of the religion of the one God, and who, lest she stir him to greater blasphemy, did not answer him present: after he departed she shook her head, to pray to God, or surely to deride his arrogance, certain of vengeance. Not himself in person, but through his servants, so that the arrogance might be greater, he blasphemed the Lord.
19.23: 19.23 High. The same. The height of mountains and the ridges of Lebanon, the tall cedars and firs. Or by metaphor it is to be taken of all the nations and their princes. Or of Jerusalem, which is Lebanon, the cedars and firs, the mighty and the nobles.
19.24: 19.24 And I have dried up. The same. Either by the multitude of the army he dried up all the streams, so that he was compelled to dig wells for himself. Or every people, which the waters signify, is laid waste by his army.
19.25: 19.25 Hast thou not? The same. This is from the person of the Lord, etc., until that he may tame thy ferocity and bring thee back among the Assyrians.
19.29: 19.29 This shall be a sign. The same. Of those things which I foretell, etc., until indeed the zeal with which he was zealous for his people against the wicked. Eat. Isaiah thus: Eat this year such things as spring of themselves, and in the second year fruits. But in the third year sow and reap, plant vineyards and eat the fruit of them. And that which shall be saved of the house of Judah, and that is left, shall take root downward, and bear fruit upward. For out of Jerusalem shall come a remnant, and that which shall be saved out of mount Sion: the zeal of the Lord of hosts shall do this (Isaiah 37). All things having been laid waste by the army, eat what could germinate again, or what could escape between the hooves of horses. In the second year, what springs up of itself without labour. Or this was said in pretence, because they thought they would perish of hunger.
19.34: 19.34 And for David my servant. RABANUS. By hope of future things he shakes off present fear. He says that they are preserved not by their own merit but by the clemency of God, and even by the memory of their father David: in which they are reminded both of their own negligence and of his faith and justice, because God so loves justice that he protects the descendants by the virtue of their forebears.
19.35: 19.35 It came to pass therefore. RABANUS. So many are slain by one angel in one night, and cruel death runs about without wounds. Concerning which in Chronicles it is read: And the Lord sent an angel, who destroyed every mighty man and warrior, and the prince of the army of the Assyrians. And he returned with shame into his own country. He who was preserved, that he might become a witness of the majesty of him whom a little before he had despised.
19.37: 19.37 And as he was worshipping in the temple. RABANUS. As though he were bringing home victory over enemies, the despiser of the true God is slaughtered in the shrine of a false deity: nor did he perish by the angelic sword, which was common, but by the parricide of his sons. The same. Pharaoh also is preserved through the ten plagues of Egypt, that he might perish last. Into the land of the Armenians. Ararat is a region in level Armenia, through which the Araxes flows, of incredible fertility, at the roots of Mount Taurus. Therefore the ark of Noah also was not carried to the mountains of Armenia generally, but to the highest mountains of Taurus, which overhangs the plains of Ararat.
20.1: 20.1 In those days. RABANUS, on the book of Kings, vol. 3. Lest the heart of Hezekiah be lifted up after his incredible triumphs, he is visited with bodily sickness and hears that he will die, so that, turning to the Lord, he may bend the sentence. God, foreknowing before the ages all that would follow, decreed how things should be ordered through the ages. It is therefore fixed how much one lives temporally in this mortal life itself. For although God added fifteen years to Hezekiah, yet when he permitted him to die, then he foreknew that he would die. When the sentence of death was spoken to him, at once at his tears life was added. At that time he deserved to die, who, puffed up, did not give thanks to the Lord for the unexpected victory, namely because he ascribed it to his own justice and merits. Nor was the term of life fixed in God's foreknowledge prolonged, but what he had lost by sinning was restored from God's generosity. When he foretold that he would die, he foreknew his penance. He turned his face to the wall of the temple, because he could not go to the temple. He says the wall of the temple, next to which the palace was, or simply to the wall, so as not to show his tears to those standing by, that he might beseech God with his whole mind.
20.2: 20.2 Who turned. RABANUS. A happy conscience, etc., until for God weighs the words of each from their heart.
20.3: 20.3 And Hezekiah wept. The same. He wept because of the promise of the Lord, etc., until and we read that very many were raised after death.
20.7: 20.7 Bring me a lump. RABANUS. The word shechin or shin, as the Hebrews say, sounds ulcer, not wound: the latter is inflicted, the former arises of itself. For Aquila, Symmachus and Theodotion have rendered it aroc, which they understand as the royal disease, to which are thought contrary whatever sweet things are taken as food or applied to the body. The power of God is therefore shown, when health is restored through harmful things. Others suspect shin to be an abscess, when the swelling body is filled with cooked and putrefying pus. And according to the art of physicians, all the matter is drawn to the surface of the skin by dry crushed figs. RABANUS. A sign is given that the sun return ten degrees, etc., until and for those living by the eighth day through the resurrection of Christ the spans of life are prolonged in place of the span of life. The same. Some transfer the ten degrees of lines to the mystery of Christ, etc., until and illumined all that shadow of the law with the rays of truth.
20.12: 20.12 At that time. The same. Above it is read, etc., until they believed him to be adored more than a man. RABANUS. The Hebrews relate, etc., until might be brought to the knowledge of men through the deed of a wicked work. The same. Hypocrites also fall away after great virtues, because they do not wish to be concealed in those virtues: who, while at the urging of malignant spirits they yield to boasting, as it were open the door to the enemies, by which they lose what they have long gathered, whence: He delivered their strength into captivity. Paul recalls his glory as the testimony of his conscience, because he does not seek the favour of another's mouth. What we do must therefore be hidden, lest, carrying it incautiously on the journey of this life, we lose it by the incursion of robbing spirits. The same. He is silent about that for which he feared offence, that he had shown them all that he had in his power, among which the chief was the furniture of the temple.
20.13: 20.13 And Hezekiah was glad at their coming. The same. The words of Chronicles say of Hezekiah, etc., until and he showed them the house of aromatics, etc. The house of aromatics, and the gold and silver. The same. Some think it was the sepulchres of the kings, which were full of aromatics, because the bodies of kings were anciently embalmed with ointments. Others rather understand it to have been a storeroom of aromatics in the temple of the Lord, where sweet-smelling spices were stored, from which the incense offered in the temple of the Lord was made. There was nothing which Hezekiah showed them not in, etc., which among the Hebrews is frequently taken to mean that he did not show them in his house and in all his power. Whence the most just anger of God, since he showed not only his treasures and those of the palace but also those of the temple, which was certainly in his power, from whose doors of the court he had earlier taken plates.
20.14: 20.14 They came from a far country. RABANUS. As if he said: The farther the land from which they came, the more glorious am I on whose account they came. To me from Babylon. He ought to have said: to glorify God for the greatness of the sign.
20.21: 20.21 And Hezekiah slept with his fathers, etc. In Chronicles it is said that Hezekiah was buried above the sepulchres of the kings, because his sepulchre was built higher on account of the piety with which he worshipped God.
21.1: 21.1 RABANUS. In whose time Isaiah, as the Hebrews relate, was sawn in two with a wooden saw, because he had called them princes of Sodom, and they turned against him as a charge that he had said: I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne high and elevated (Isaiah 6), God having said: Man shall not see me and live (Exodus 33). The same. Manasseh turned to idols and abominations. God or the Lord spoke to him, but he would not give heed; therefore, conquered, he was led to Babylon; in distress he prayed to the Lord intently and did great penance, and his prayer was heard, and he brought him back to his kingdom, and Manasseh knew that the Lord he is God. Therefore after crimes committed let no one despair of the mercy of God, but rather have hope of pardon through penance.
21.24: 21.24 Josiah. RABANUS. Josiah corrected all the filth of idols, and exercised himself vigorously in the worship of God, as was foretold of him long before through the prophet.
22.14: 22.14 In the Second. RABANUS. In Chronicles it is read of Hezekiah that he built up all the wall that had been broken down, and another wall without; whence Zephaniah: A howling from the Second. The prophetess therefore dwelt in the Second, that is, in the part of the second wall.
23.10: 23.10 He defiled. RABANUS, on the book of Kings, vol. 3. Josiah defiled Topheth, scattering there the bones of the dead as he is read to have done in the following places, or any other unclean things, so that the place might appear fit for abomination rather than delight to all who looked upon it. In the valley. The same. The valley of Hinnom is next to the wall of Jerusalem toward the east, etc., until because Topheth is called breadth.
23.11: 23.11 He took away. RABANUS. The Jews had given themselves up to the superstitions of the nations, who among other things are accustomed to paint or make an image of the sun as a beardless boy, because no old age comes on it through the ages, born daily in a new rising. To it they assign a chariot and horses, because Elijah was taken up to heaven in a fiery chariot and fiery horses, which among other things they see painted on a wall, and are deceived by the nearness of the name: for in Greek the sun is called Helios.
23.13: 23.13 The high places. RABANUS. Scripture means places set on leafy hills, in which they sacrificed either to demons, or to the Lord, enticed by the pleasantness of the places, contrary to the prohibition, leaving the altar which was in the temple, they flocked thither to offer: whence it is said so often in this book of the less perfect kings: But the high places he took not away. Which he had built. The same. Here it is shown that Solomon never perfectly repented of the crime of idolatry he had committed: for if he had truly repented, he would have taken care before all things that the idols which he had built be removed from the city: and not leave as if wisely done, to the scandal of the foolish, things he himself, though most wise, had made in error. And Chemosh. RABANUS. Elsewhere it is read that Solomon built a shrine of Chemosh on the mountain which is over against Jerusalem. But there is no contradiction; because that mountain was in such close neighbourhood to the city that it seemed to belong to it, and to defile it with the filth that was heaped up on it. The abomination of Moab. The same. The idols are called offence, because either God is offended by them, or they bring offence and ruin to their worshippers.
23.16: 23.16 He took the bones, etc. Josiah commanded the bones of the dead to be burned on the altar, because their sacrifices were profane, and through the error of idolatry they not only offered cattle to demons but handed themselves over to the power of demons: because by the just judgment of God they were to be scattered together with the altar which they had made for idols. Mystically, those who, given over to the service of the devil, end a sacrilegious life in time will be consumed in eternal torments, God repaying according to deserts.
23.21: 23.21 Keep the phase. RABANUS. Josiah holds the type of the Saviour, etc., until and to you that fear, the sun of justice shall arise. For there was not kept such a phase, etc. Because, the figures being taken away, on the day of judgment the saints will pass from death to life, and so will rejoice in the sight of their Creator, because the God of gods shall be seen in Sion. RABANUS. That Josiah, having cast out of the land the idols, pythons, soothsayers and all uncleannesses, is read to have celebrated the phase of the Lord, teaches morally that we should first purge the land of the heart of vices, that we may be able to serve God, and so celebrate the pasch pleasing to the Lord: Not with the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth (1 Corinthians 5). The same. Josiah was wounded in the field of Megiddo, whence he died at once. And the people mourned him greatly, Jeremiah especially. For then he is said to have lamented thus: How doth the city sit solitary! Of this lamentation it is said: In that day there shall be a great lamentation in Jerusalem, as the lamentation of Hadadrimmon, which is the name of the king who then reigned in Carchemish, to whose help Josiah had come against Necho king of Egypt. The same. The killing of Josiah by Pharaoh Necho, done at Megiddo, signifies the persecution of the ancient enemy against the preachers, whom through envy he strives to give over to death, and endeavours to take from the land of the Church: that he may more easily scatter the whole people. Pharaoh scattering, Necho a striking, Megiddo from temptation. The devil, permitted to rise against the saints, here contends with all his strength, that by tempting he may strike and scatter the flock of the Lord, and take away first those by whose comfort they were to have been helped to fight against the enemy.
23.30: 23.30 Jehoahaz the son of Josiah. The same. By another name he is called Shallum, but because he was most perverse, he reigned a short time, for Necho bound him, because the people had made him king against his will, and led him into Egypt. The same. Jehoahaz detained signifies bad teachers, whom the people of the land, namely those given to earthly cupidity, elect as prelates, consenting to their vices, whom Pharaoh bound in Riblah, when the devil, enervating through a multitude of flatterers, deceives the hearts of prelates, and so plunges into the dark abyss those bound in the spiritual Egypt with the chains of sins.
23.35: 23.35 But the silver and gold he gave, etc. The same. The wicked one demands the tribute of his service from the carnal people, that they may be ready in all things to obey him in both thought and speech. Jehoiakim exacts the tribute at the king's command, because the devil through masters devoted to him demands from each to pay according to his strength the tribute of sin, and so daily prepares destruction in the wickedly set over subjects.
24.1: 24.1 RABANUS. When anyone has once given himself over to any vice, etc., until and implore help from God. RABANUS. Josephus relates that he was killed by Nebuchadnezzar and cast out before the walls of Jerusalem unburied, of whom it had been foretold: He shall be buried with the burial of an ass (Jeremiah 22). And Jehoiakim reigned, etc. The same. The name Jehoiakim is written differently when the father is designated, who is also Eliakim: differently when the son is signified, who is also Jeconiah; for when it denotes the father it is written with k and m; when the son, with ch and n.
24.8: 24.8 Jerusalem. BEDE, on the book of Kings, question 30, vol. 2. Jerusalem and the land of Israel, etc., until that is, spiritual knowledge is turned to the works of sinners.
24.14: 24.14 The same, ibid. The craftsman and the smith, and nothing was left, except the poor of the people of the land. RABANUS, from Bede, ibid. What above the Philistines are narrated to have done to the people of Israel, when it is said: There was no smith found in all the land of Israel, for the Philistines had taken care lest the Hebrews should make them a sword or a spear to fight (1 Kings 13), so now the Chaldeans strive that none remain in it, craftsman or smith, who could rebuild or repair the ruined walls of the city. RABANUS. Evil are the rulers who abuse the gift and endowment of God, and falsely usurp for themselves the name of justice. For Mattaniah is interpreted gift, or endowment: Zedekiah, the Lord just. He reigned eleven years, because he was a transgressor of the law, which is signified by the number ten. Nine, which has less than ten, signifies the imperfection of the law, as eleven the transgression. Rightly, therefore, Nebuchadnezzar in the ninth year of the reign of Zedekiah besieged the city in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month: because evil pastors, when they neglect to perfect in work and teaching the commandments of the decalogue, which they hold by knowledge, it is necessary that the ancient enemy with his army surround with siege the people committed to them, and enclose them by the fortification of error and vices built up, encircling the city: and so famine prevails in the city, famine indeed of the word of God, when the bread of doctrine is not dispensed to the people of the land.
25.4: 25.4 And it was broken up, etc. RABANUS. Broken indeed, by the various temptations of demons, is the guard of the peoples, etc., until who is burdened by wicked custom and the multitude of his iniquity.
25.8: 25.8 In the fifth month. RABANUS. The order of the time agrees with the reason of the vengeance. In the fifth month the city was laid waste which despised keeping the Pentateuch of the law, and on the seventh day of the month, because it did not keep the rest of the sabbath, and acted contrary to the commandments of God, vainly flattering itself on the security of dwelling in holy places. The same. Nebuzaradan came, which is interpreted winnowing-fan, or prophecy of another's judgment, etc., until but thorns and thistles of vices rather grow up.
25.13: 25.13 And the brazen pillars which, etc. The same. And the bases we understand as teachers, who by the sonority of preaching and the firmness of faith ought to have sustained others. The brazen sea: the washing of baptism, or the compunction of tears. All these the spiritual Chaldeans, through the sloth of the masters, strive to take away from the house of the Lord and to break.
25.14: 25.14 The pots also. The same. Because, taking away from the service of God the diverse offices in the ecclesiastical orders, they turned them to their own most wicked use.
25.15: 25.15 The censers and bowls. When they overturn, by hindering, the prayer by which the divinity could be appeased and the cup of the word by which the weary ought to be refreshed. The same. Because the wicked enemy strives to take away from the house of the Lord both the precious sense and the beauty of eloquence, and to lead them with himself to confusion.
25.18: 25.18 He took also. The same. The devil strives to deceive in the Church not only the common people but the strong and princes, and to take sinners captive, whence in Job of him: His meat is choice (Job 33). He took Seraiah, which is interpreted bound, the first priest, when the first order of the Church, which is in the bishops, he constrains by the chain of vices through love of earthly pleasure. Likewise Zephaniah, which is interpreted hidden, the second priest, when he subjects to his dominion men of the second order, that is, priests, who digging in the earth had hidden the talent of the word. And three doorkeepers, who ought to have opened the door of faith, and holding the key of knowledge neither entered themselves nor allowed others to enter. The eunuch signifies the foolish virgins, who held vessels empty of oil in their hands, abstaining from bodily union, and yet not willing to have the oil of grace and mercy in their breast. They are set in vain over the warriors, since they do not guard against arrogance. Five men of those who stood before the king (Matthew 5), that is, those who, serving pleasure by the five senses of the body, always stood by the king of vices. Sopher the prince. The same. It is interpreted scattering or dividing: signifying those who, scattering the untaught in the Church, whom they ought to have trained for the warfare of Christ, by wicked examples, separate them from the company of the faithful through error. And sixty men of the common people, that is, foolish workers, who are deservedly of the common people, because they neglected to learn divine counsels and fulfil them in deeds. And sixty men. The same. All these Nebuzaradan led to the king of Babylon, and they were killed, because the devil seeks to bring the prey which he has torn from the Church to the slaughter of perpetual death: whom the king of confusion strikes at Riblah, that is, in the multitude of crimes and love of pleasures. The same. When those who seemed to have the confession of the name of God in the Church are, through manifold crimes, transferred from the land of the living and led away into the kingdom of confusion and error, etc., until and to contemplate the face of our Creator for ever.
25.23: 25.23 And Seraiah. The son of Seraiah the priest was preserved, and the father was killed. From him in the captivity was afterwards born Jesus the great priest, who brought back the people with Zerubbabel.
